why power isnt about control the psychology of perception that actually works over the past year ive been obsessively researching social dynamics status hierarchies and what actually makes someone powerful in modern society not because i wanted to manipulate people or become some corporate overlord but because i noticed something weird the people who seemed most desperate to control situations were often the least respected while those who barely seemed to try commanded rooms effortlessly that paradox drove me down a rabbit hole of psychology research anthropology studies and countless books on influence and power dynamics heres what most people get wrong about power we think its about authority dominance making others do what we want but real power operates on a completely different frequency its not about forcing compliance its about shaping reality itself in other peoples minds the moment you understand this distinction everything about social dynamics starts making sense true power lives entirely in other peoples perceptions of you this isnt some woo woo mindset stuff robert greene breaks this down brilliantly in the 48 laws of power over 12 million copies sold considered the definitive modern text on power dynamics greene spent years studying historical figures con artists and leaders and the pattern is undeniable those who tried to maintain power through pure force eventually lost it while those who mastered perception kept it indefinitely the book is dense and sometimes morally grey but it reveals uncomfortable truths about how humans actually operate in hierarchies this completely changed how i understood workplace politics and even friendships best book on strategic thinking ive ever encountered think about it a ceo doesnt personally control every employees actions they cant physically force anyone to show up monday morning their power exists because everyone collectively agrees it does because of how theyre perceived within the organizational structure the second that perception shifts their power evaporates regardless of their title weve all seen this happen when a respected leader gets exposed for something that destroys their credibility the formal authority remains but the real power vanishes instantly status is performed not possessed youve probably noticed this at parties or social gatherings theres always someone who walks in and just commands attention without saying a word meanwhile someone else might be desperately trying to prove their worth through stories and accomplishments and it lands flat the difference the first person has internalized that their value doesnt need constant validation theyre comfortable with silence comfortable taking up space comfortable being unimpressive for stretches because theyre not performing for approval anthropologist david graeber explored this extensively before his death his work on bureaucracy and power structures showed that many powerful positions exist primarily as theater elaborate performances that maintain collective belief systems when you stop performing the role convincingly the power disappears its why politicians obsess over image management and why corporate leaders hire expensive consultants to help them project authority i started testing this in low stakes situations instead of trying to be the smartest person in meetings i focused on being the calmest instead of rushing to fill silences i got comfortable with pauses instead of over explaining my decisions i stated them simply and moved on the shift in how people responded was genuinely surprising not because i was manipulating anyone but because id stopped signaling insecurity your reaction to challenges broadcasts your actual power level this ones huge when someone disrespects you or questions your competence your immediate response reveals everything if you get defensive aggressive or try desperately to prove yourself youre confirming their frame that youre beneath them youre accepting their right to judge you insanely powerful people dont do this they either ignore challenges completely signaling theyre beneath notice or respond with such calm certainty that the challenger looks foolish for even trying theres a whole chapter in the like switch by jack schafer former fbi behavioral analyst about this dynamic schafer spent decades studying how to build rapport and influence often in hostile situations his framework shows that perceived power correlates directly with how little you need from others emotionally neediness destroys power instantly because it positions you as the one seeking validation the book focuses on practical techniques for influence without manipulation which honestly more people should read because it makes you hyper aware of when others are using these tactics on you scarcity amplifies perception ever notice how the friend whos always available gets taken for granted while the one whos genuinely busy gets more respect and attention its not fair but its consistent when youre constantly accessible constantly trying to add value constantly available to help youre inadvertently signaling low status high status people are gatekeepers of their own time and attention they dont need to be everywhere because their presence itself has value this doesnt mean becoming a flaky asshole who ghosts everyone it means being genuinely selective about where you invest energy and not apologizing for having boundaries i used to say yes to every social invitation every favor request every meeting suggestion because i thought thats what good people do then i realized i was training everyone that my time had no value when i started declining things without elaborate justifications peoples respect actually increased befreed is an ai learning app that turns books research papers and expert content into personalized audio and adaptive learning plans based on what matters to you a columbia grad who used to work at google helped build it which shows in the quality what makes it different is the depth control you can get a 10minute overview of key concepts or switch to a 40minute deep dive with actual examples and context when something clicks it pulls from verified sources like academic research and expert talks so the content stays grounded the learning plan adapts as you go tracking what resonates and adjusting recommendations accordingly theres also a voice assistant you can interrupt midsession to ask questions or explore tangents which feels more like an actual conversation than passive listening the power paradox is that pursuing it directly repels it the people most transparently hungry for status validation and control are the ones who never get it or lose it quickly if they do you can smell desperation from a mile away that try hard energy that makes everyone uncomfortable real power comes from having a secure enough sense of self that you dont need external validation to feel okay which sounds like a catch 22 but its not you build that security through competence through surviving setbacks through gradually proving to yourself that youre resilient regardless of others opinions psychologist dacher keltner researches this at berkeley he literally calls it the power paradox people gain power through qualities like empathy collaboration and social intelligence but once they have power they often lose those exact qualities and start acting entitled selfish and tone deaf then they lose the power its a cycle that plays out everywhere from tech startups to political dynasties strategic vulnerability is more powerful than invulnerability this seems counterintuitive but its backed by solid research bren browns work on shame and vulnerability shows that leaders who occasionally show appropriate weakness are actually perceived as more confident and trustworthy than those who maintain perfect facades why because denying all vulnerability signals fragility like youre so insecure that even admitting minor flaws would shatter you meanwhile selectively sharing struggles signals youre secure enough to be honest key word strategic trauma dumping on acquaintances or constantly complaining isnt powerful its exhausting but admitting when you dont know something acknowledging mistakes without excessive apology sharing relevant failures that taught you something these actually elevate your status because they demonstrate security power requires managing others emotional states not controlling their actions this is where most people completely miss the point they think power means getting people to comply with demands real power means people wanting to comply because youve created an environment where thats the appealing option its the difference between fear based compliance fragile resentment inducing temporary and genuine influence sustainable multiplying resilient the best managers ive worked for never had to pull rank or make threats they created conditions where doing good work felt meaningful and where people genuinely wanted their approval thats infinitely more powerful than authority based on consequences you can build this through genuine interest in others through creating psychological safety through demonstrating competence consistently look none of this means being fake or calculating in some sociopathic way its actually the opposite the most sustainable form of power comes from being genuinely grounded genuinely competent genuinely okay with yourself that security naturally manifests in behaviors that others perceive as powerful calm under pressure comfortable with conflict unbothered by tests selective with attention start paying attention to who commands respect in your environments and why usually its not the loudest person or the one with the fanciest title its someone whos mastered the perception game often without consciously realizing it thats your template not to copy them exactly but to identify the principles theyre embodying that you can adapt to your authentic self

daily reading article for varc practice english ivy often admired for its lush green foliage and ability to climb walls or decorate indoor spaces may offer more than just aesthetic value it could act as a highly effective natural air purifier this insight comes from a preliminary study presented at the american college of allergy asthma and immunology acaai annual meeting held in anaheim california in 2005 the research conducted by hilary spyersduran fnp and her colleague at west coast clinical trials aimed to explore whether english ivy could help clean indoor air contaminated with harmful biological particles to simulate reallife indoor pollution the researchers placed moldy bread and canine feces into enclosed glass containers creating an environment rich in airborne mold spores and fecal particles both of which are known to contribute to poor air quality and can trigger allergies asthma or other respiratory issues into these challenging conditions they introduced english ivy plants to observe any potential changes in air quality what they found was striking within just 12 hours the presence of english ivy led to a 785 reduction in airborne mold particles and a 9425 decrease in airborne fecal matter these results suggest that the plant has a powerful ability to absorb or break down bioaerosols tiny biological particles that float in the air and can have adverse effects on human health while the findings are promising and suggest potential for using english ivy as a natural method to reduce exposure to harmful indoor pollutants there are several caveats the study has not undergone peer review meaning the results have not yet been scrutinized and validated by the broader scientific community moreover the controlled conditions under which the experiment was conducted may not exactly replicate the complexities of realworld indoor environments where airflow humidity temperature and other variables could influence the plants effectiveness another important consideration is safety although english ivy may help purify the air the plant itself is toxic if ingested it contains compounds like saponins and polyacetylene compounds that can cause serious gastrointestinal distress in both humans and animals therefore while english ivy could be useful in outdoor settings especially in areas where animal waste is more prevalent or carefully monitored indoor environments it should always be kept out of reach of children and pets despite these limitations this study opens up intriguing possibilities for further research into how common houseplants might contribute to healthier indoor air particularly in settings with limited ventilation or elevated biological pollutants as concerns about air quality and respiratory health grow especially in urban or petowning households such natural solutions could become a valuable part of a broader strategy for maintaining clean and safe living environments

like a stormy lake sean and i watched the drivers abilities with critical interest nodding our approval or disgust at each darting move as the pale green bulb in the intersection ahead turned monochrome then red the driver geared down and attempted to slow but the weighted rear chucked us over the crosswalk and into the intersection with necksnapping acceleration our driver thrust ahead through nothing resembling enough space in the crosstraffic horns of various pitches did their best to warn us of the impending proliferation of scrap metal our taxis transmission could be heard ripping through the gears like itd been locked in a bullpen and kicked in the balls this was moscows rush hour and we made him spend 40 minutes fighting it dad meanwhile was oblivious to it all lost in a happy place he gazed out the window at the passing city sometimes his head would roll back as we turned rapidly so all he could see was the ceiling i know dad and insofar as he was concerned the driving was in the drivers hands soon enough the taxi slid into a chiropractic uturn and rode up onto the curb in front of yaroslavl station home to our departure a keenly swift porter lodged a trolley under the bumper where the driver was dropping our belongings since the taxis fee had been included in our arrangements the awkward time came to say spacibo and he got a maple leaf pin he said something about me and my mother and drove off the porter inched the cart away from the taxi and disappeared into a crowd of many thousands of bustling travellers we gave chase he hadnt gotten far when we tracked him down and anxiously counted our bags the throngs grew in intensity as we cornered around the back from its south side babushkas dragged large expandable plastic cubes of clothes and toiletries young men stood in groups keenly watching for a friend or more likely for a hole in the defence system of foreigners a dancing placard read 316 intermittently we were afforded a view of set upon set of tracks stretching into the western horizon where the sun was slipping down its wall of light above the commotion the fur hats and tight scarves in front of each track terminus scrolled the destinations of minsk st petersburg and omsk intercity electrichka destined for tver vladimir and bryansk awaited the nightly rush of rumps passengers were pulling themselves up onto carriage decks arguing with station attendants studying their tickets and dragging their lives behind them along the platform i knew i was becoming romantically involved with russia the porter slammed the cart through a set of doors and stopped in front of a large uniformed woman at a turnstile our boarding passes were produced for the first of so many times and we were deemed worthy of entry our bags were hoisted off im two im three im two then we were in and the dimness of the cavernous station overtook us endless lines of imposing benches were occupied by hundreds of old russian women for the first time in russia i saw asians separated from one another by stacked boxes crates and cubes of wrapped clothing in an empty corner a pyramid was fashioned from our belongings dad and sean set off to use the telephone bank while i squatted defensively beside our bags two babushkas leaned into each other discussing something with great fervor some children played tag around their familys trunks screaming cheerfully at each successful attempt at eluding that hound at the heels touch of the pursuer one child stood silently watching his arm wrapped tight around his mothers calf his other entire hand was being used as a pacifier some old women dressed in black were crossing themselves in the north corner one covering her face in silent sobs was being consoled by another with small pats rising from the longest wall in phosphorescent redpinned lettering hung that quintessential railway station device and travellers beacon the departures and arrivals board it announced the location of every train bound in or out from and to everywhere a fuzzy transformation threw up new destinations and rid the black screen of news of recent arrivals peking our first train and inevitably our last city was scheduled to leave in fortyfive minutes from track seven the rossiya the name given to the transsiberian famed trekker of the motherland was due anytime my stomach ached with anticipation a public address system with an overpowering trebled feedback repeated its announcement of the next departure and three subsequent arrivals i recounted the baggage to kill some time seven i did it again seven i did it again seven the paranoid traveler courts confidence in the oddest ways dad and sean emerged from the crowd mumbling something to the effect of first in space and you cant even get a telephone line out with their return i was free to check outside for our trains arrival all three times track seven was vacant ten minutes before its scheduled departure i noticed it berthed at the station and ran to my team flailing about like id taken a hit of dc current our seven bags count em again were scooped up and taken to the door and into a funnel of traffic at the turnstiles where the crowd stopped any movement there above the heads and ushanka fur hats sat the rossiya stretching far into the suburban land of tracks an old porter smaller than all but two of the bags encouraged us to use his assistance bilyeta he said he wants our tickets i said looking to dad and sean what for dunno pachemoo i joined the porters knotted eyes poezduh he enunciated with an emphesis placed duh vagon train i translated wagon he wants to know our train number what wagon are we in sean interrupted thinking he was helping da shtoy vagon the porter waved a mitted fist at all of us though i took it most personally we frantically located the tickets in our pockets and hip packs and passed them to the porter his mitt ran a thick finger over the ticket and he hummed as though a secret number was encrypted in the printing it was a handwritten ticket they all were in the late twentieth century someone was still writing out documents by hand vosyem eight he pushed the cart ahead of us as he hollered to the platform full of people to mind their bodies and baggage a locomotive in quick enginepulsing revolutions rode to the empty dock on our right faces ducked to the windows looking for loved ones or checking on the weather a conductor stood a step down waiting to draw out the stairs trudging past our own behemoth we gazed happily at the cyrillic signs in which held moskva peking was stencilled black on white the hordes of people thinned as the porter halted and began unloading our seven bags at wagon eight a chugging idle rose from beneath the carriage two chinese officials in heavy decorated coats sized us up all we knew about our accommodations was that we had reserved three beds in a fourperson berth to irkutsk some four days away our reservations had been made in vancouver by an agent whod been briefed that wed like to keep it affordable and thus could live without certain amenities we were now concerned about who would be occupying the fourth bed and our remaining breathing space as the chinese officials deliberated a young russian man inebriated enough to stagger joined our group hollering a good lungful of vodkalaced air he spoke insistently and with the snide confidence offered by his consumption i lost any ability to translate at the slightest slur and instead guessed along with the others that this was our roommate the shorter of the two chinese men spoke in a quick and strong tone to which the drunk reacted by producing a crumpled ticket the perusal stole a heartstopping minute after which an official arm was pointed far down to the last few cars with that to our great relief the drunk staggered off until the crowd enveloped him a whistle sounded from a train some tracks over and the platform vibrated lightly as it pushed away the chinese officials finally smiled and shook dads hand and one swung a reflexive arm inwards preese wekom we hoisted our luggage inside the vestibule our compartment was the closest to the far end of the car the last of eight such rooms some bagbanging distance away one official slid open the door to our temporary tenement to siberia spacious enough for one close for two tight for three and something like pow conditions for four dad and sean fought ahead of me to load the cabin and claim bunk rights the chinese man rubbed his cheek indicative of problem solving and slid open the door to the next berth encouraging me in with preese wekom i took no time in getting down to the matter at hand i set out to make my room look as inhospitable as possible to any passerby contemplating cohabitation i opened every zipper placed perishables bruisedsideup about the table crushed a brandname cola can on the floor unscrewed a light bulb and began disrobing i put my ear to the thin wall to hear the harsh utterances as dad and sean fought like brothers next door a moment later seans face loaded with suspicion appeared in my doorway dad come take a look at this i dumped my backpacks contents as a barricade should either relative attempt entry and adjusted my underwear dads face now sat above seans what are you doing son the chinese guy gave it to me a whole cabin he asked i prefer couchette b3 the b is for bling but yes the whole thing they looked at each other and dad left he snores you know sean said watching dad amble back he was about to imply that we should work something out but i pulled a quick ploy from my files primogeniture what he seemed perplexed it means first born miata right to inheritance et cetera et al as in born birth first one me my berth i smiled the tugoflip smirk of someone whod breezed into mensa i call it heir superiority you are with him if i was a monkey id throw feces at you i am a cruel person dad screams in his sleep youre a greedy selfish synonym you are a prop in my movie in the corridor we opened the heavy window halfway and looked out onto the platform the sunlight was creating long shadows commotion at the far rear of the train was still being dealt with by passengers and porters as the clock began nudging the departure time of 1950 the chinese official whod welcomed us on board had shed his overcoat brought up the stairs with an ironlevered clunk and closed the outer door sealing off the physical entities of moscow we commented on the lack of people joining us in the vestibule to bid us farewell no matter it was one of the proudest moments of our lives then the first whisper of motion the platform inched backwards and we gained a hint of momentum it ran beside us as our pace quickened the porters the people the commotion and the station began falling away behind us this is our moment dad yelled as much to the moscovian night as to sean and me it was we all held those few seconds as one would cradle an oscar the trains speed picked up the doubleslips and crossovers the whispering wheel assemblies and the ties that bind the rails rocking the wagons side to side my heart fell for russia the platform dropped off and we cheered and screamed joyous expletives out to the sea of tracks as they danced to our applause merging and dividing from each other our coach official had lost his hat rolled up his sleeves and was now walking towards us with clanking bottles of beer looking less and less official beijing beer he announced passing them around liberally and rounding up an opener he jammed a palm towards dad khan rick pleased to meet you khan sean nice meeting you sean said with an air of sophistication khan he repeated turning to me brent i said taking both his hand and the opener you are so calm he tried with a goshgeewillikers cluck thank you im not medicated or anything so calm he smiled and gurgled a throatful of beer then instantly he was gone to the other end of the coach we figured this was to let us enjoy the instant of leaving on a journey that had taken us so much to arrange this was it moscow slowly receded into a deeply silhouetted skyline of antennaed rooftops the quarter moon hung like a white sickle in the darkening sky the rossiyas speed increased furthering the euphoria fuelling our excitement and creating a fresh sharp gust of air in the corridor no one emerged from any of the compartments all the doors were now closed and curiously silent we had figured that the entire train would be crawling with people and that wed be doing shifts to guard our baggage i ventured out to the corridor to undertake a forensic analysis on the extremely unusual circumstance that we were alone in a coach in such a crowded train the final room housed khan sitting with his feet up and smoking a half hour before hed been dressed as someone who might shoot you for spite now he was looking cozy as if with all due respect he was into his third litre of with any real communication i glanced out the window to catch a deep violet sky in the clickityclackity echo it grew into night and a multitude of dazzling constellations grew from the blackness dad brushed his nose i just wanted to tell you while you were fortifying your cabin against us sean and i ran into an intourist official on the platform and he gave us some things to remember i was open watch your wallet that means hip pack as well secondly another parental finger appeared dont trust anyone i waited dad always comes in threes and thirdly brent i want you to hear me never ever drink with strangers would you mind looking at me while im talking to you i am its peripheral day in belarus im honouring that repeat them back to me he said dad in adherence i felt for my wallet as khan staggered up from behind with another round of beers and a rosy glow on his amber cheeks sean came around from the nearest washroom looking like hed just found out the truth about santa claus he was shifting his eyes quickly and it was evident that something had gotten to him what happened to you in there i asked nothing youll see no nothing ok the unspeakable khan waved us back to his cabin dad stopped us guys he was trying to slip something on us you know i cant stand the smoking so sean heres the deal we allocate brents temporary living quarters as the smoking place khan broke into song far off in his tiny room sean nodded as did i and that was that khan was in a loud crushingoftin falsetto waving his arms about in a tai chi fashion as sean and i shadowed his door a small transistor radio was tuned to one of those stations that clings to the end of the dial khan stopped as he saw our eyes surveying his compartment we were ushered in urged to sit and drink another bottle of beer for some long minutes nothing was understood though we tried access denied syntax error 404 error his face seemed to compute attempts were made and just when it seemed that the point had carried across the wire everything broke down and wed sip our beers and stare at his chinese calendar pinup khan raised his lower bunk and withdrew a small stack of stapled papers i glanced over as he began reading and wrapping his lips around some english phrases they included some attendantfocused closedend statements that had been prepared for the unlikely event of encountering englishspeaking passengers beneath each were the chinese symbols presumably telling khan what hed just said herro hello sean and i replied

new class accursed v09 a cursedriven martial class blood hunter reimagining hope everyone had a great holiday i was finally able to finish up this class which has technically been 3 years in the making starting with my blood hunter revitalized revision this rework began while i was in the middle of the revision i was unhappy with the way the lore and mechanics fought each other in certain places there were also problems with subclass progression which i skimmed over in my revision though i did try to fix some of the mechanical problems while i was doing all that the thought occurred to me why not just start over from the beginning and have both mechanics and lore a unified system that a makes sense and b works also to separate it from the theme of selfharm while still keeping the riskreward playstyle intact a couple of points im sure will get brought up 1 yes i know 68 pages is a lot actually it wil be more once i get npc statblocks done but this comes from 2 main sources first i have not only the base 4 subclasses but also a vampire and psionic sub i also have an exiled version of each of the primary classes bringing the total number of subs to 12 second im a firm believer of horizontal power i love giving players choice now thats not necessarily the 5e way of doing things but it is my way if thats not your style then feel free to move on 2 yes i also know its the name of a class by ross leiser but the two have virtually no similarities beyond the name i did try to come up with some different names but when you have a class that explores being cursed and how you use those curses theres very very limited options 3 currently the only art is the cover theres lots of blank spaces where id ideally put art but thats lower on my priority list so if you see big open spaces thats most likely the reason 4 i only showed about 5 pages in the preview to give some sampling because obviously reddit isnt about to let me post 68 pages hopefully its enough to catch interest in looking at the homebrewery or pdf docs below 5 my design profile is to balance for phb 5e14xge or low tce tce is where we started to get a lot of power creep so i try to avoid that in my designs with that said i also am working on a 5e24 version which will have some changes since i have to include things like weapon masteries so there might be some small changes so look forward to that coming in the future as always feedback is welcome if you like what you see you can also check out my website and patreon ttrpg traveller accursed homebrewery accursed pdf

balance issues why they happenand what actually helps balance issues why they happenand what actually helps balance problems are more common than most people realize they dont always mean something serious but they do signal that one or more systems in the body arent working together people describe balance issues as feeling unsteady or off wobbling when standing on one foot hesitation on stairs or uneven ground lets break this down simply balance isnt one thing its a team effort your balance depends on two main systems working together 1 the feet ankles your foundation your feet contain thousands of sensory receptors that tell your brain where you are in space how much pressure youre applying whether the ground is stable or uneven if foot muscles are weak stiff injured or desensitized from shoes injury or immobilization balance often suffers 2 the brain nervous system the integrator your brain combines signals from your feet eyes and inner ear to decide when to correct posture how fast to react how much muscle activation is needed if signals are unclear or delayed balance feels unreliable common causes of balance issues balance problems dont always come from one cause often its a combination foot or ankle injuries sprains tendonitis plantar fasciitis weak intrinsic foot muscles poor coordination or deconditioning fear of movement after injury the good news many of these are modifiable why balance often gets worse after injury or rest after injury or pain the nervous system becomes protective muscles shut down to avoid threat even once pain improves balance can lag behindbecause the system hasnt been retrained yet this is why people often say what actually helps improve balance 1 gentle progressive practice balance improves with consistent lowlevel challenge not extreme drills examples standing on one foot near support slow weight shifts controlled heeltotoe movements 2 foot awareness sensory input restoring connection between the brain and feet is key this can include barefoot balance on safe surfaces textured surfaces or simple tools the goal isnt intensityits feedback 3 intrinsic foot strength small foot muscles play a big role in stability exercises often focus on arch control toe coordination 4 patience with the nervous system balance improves before strength or after itdepending on the person progress is rarely linear and small gains matter optional educational approaches some people explore structured balancefocused programs that emphasize foot sensory work coordination progressive stability challenges one example often mentioned online is neuro balance therapy which is framed as an educational approach not a medical treatment some people use this type of method to help rebuild balance confidence after injury or long periods of inactivity its optionalbut it reflects an important principle balance is trained not just rested key takeaways quick read balance relies on feet inner ear and brain working together injuries commonly disrupt balance pain relief doesnt always mean balance is restored gentle consistent balance work is more effective than aggressive training want to learn more if youre interested in understanding why your balance feels off learning simple safe ways to retrain it exploring optional educational tools and programs you can visit my blog on my hocoos website to read more or explore additional resources at your own pace click here to learn more educationfirst no pressure

most people wont change because they think they already know who they are ive spent the last year diving deep into self transformation stuff books podcasts research papers youtube rabbit holes all because i noticed something weird everyone talks about wanting to change but like 95 of people stay exactly the same year after year and its not laziness its something way more interesting most of us are walking around wearing an identity we built in high school or college and were defending it like our life depends on it we say things like im just not a morning person or ive always been anxious like these are facts about our dna instead of just patterns we got really good at the wild part weve accumulated so much evidence to support these beliefs that changing feels like lying about who we are but heres what neuroscience and behavioral psychology keep proving your personality isnt a fixed thing its more like a muscle that youve been training in one specific direction for years you can retrain it you just need the right framework stop trying to find yourself and start building yourself this is probably the most liberating concept ive encountered dan koe talks about this extensively in his content and its backed by decades of identity research youre not discovering some hidden authentic self buried under layers of trauma and societal expectations youre literally creating yourself in real time through the choices you make daily the person you are right now is just the sum of repeated thoughts and behaviors change those change everything the problem is were terrified of this freedom because it means were responsible its way easier to say this is just who i am than to admit this is who ive been choosing to be rewrite your internal narrative obsessively your brain has this voice thats been narrating your life for years and its probably kind of a dick it says things like you always mess this up or youre not the type of person who does that these arent truths theyre just stories youve been telling yourself so many times they feel true cognitive behavioral therapy research shows that changing these automatic thoughts literally rewires your brain over time start catching these narratives and asking is this actually true or is this just familiar then deliberately replace them if you think im bad with money start saying im learning to manage money better sounds cheesy but the data on positive psychology and neural plasticity is pretty clear here the alter ego effect by todd herman is legitimately fascinating for this hermans a performance coach whos worked with olympic athletes and fortune 500 executives the book breaks down how adopting an alter ego isnt fake or delusional its actually a psychological tool that helps you bypass limiting beliefs he uses research from embodied cognition to explain why professional athletes often have pregame rituals or personas when youre being someone else your brain doesnt trigger the same fear responses and selfsabotaging patterns it creates psychological distance from your current identity so you can act differently this book will make you question everything you think about authenticity i genuinely think its one of the most practical psychology books out there for people who feel trapped by their own personality design your environment like its a product youre building james clears work on this is solid your environment is constantly voting on who you become if you want to be someone who reads more put books everywhere and hide your phone if you want to be healthier make the default option in your kitchen nutritious food environmental design research from behavioral economics shows that were way more influenced by whats immediately available than we think youre not going to willpower your way into being a different person you need to make the new behaviors so stupid easy that youd have to actively resist them remove friction from good habits add friction to bad ones your willpower is a limited resource so stop relying on it the psychology of money by morgan housel isnt really about finance its about how we make decisions and why were so irrational about our own behavior housel is a former wall street journal columnist and the book won like every personal finance book award in 2020 whats brilliant about it is how he breaks down the stories we tell ourselves about success failure and worth he shows how our relationship with money reveals our deepest beliefs about ourselves and our future if youre trying to recreate yourself you need to understand the psychological patterns driving your choices this applies way beyond money reading it made me realize how many logical decisions i was making were actually just emotional reactions id rationalized insanely good read for understanding your own psychology build in public and create accountability structures this is something thats been huge in the online entrepreneur space when you declare who youre becoming publicly you create social pressure that actually works in your favor start a blog post on social media tell friends your goals research on commitment devices shows that public commitment increases followthrough rates significantly but heres the key dont just announce goals document the process share the struggles the incremental progress the setbacks this does two things it makes failure more uncomfortable so youre less likely to quit and it starts building evidence for your new identity every time you post about your progress youre reinforcing to yourself im the kind of person who does this you can also use apps like forfeit which lets you set financial stakes for your habits you commit money that gets donated to a cause you hate if you dont follow through sounds extreme but loss aversion is one of the strongest psychological motivators we have or try complice which is designed around coworking and accountability partnerships the social element makes a massive difference befreed is an aipowered learning app that pulls from highquality sources like books research papers and expert talks to create personalized podcasts tailored to your specific goals built by a team from columbia university and google it lets you customize everything from a quick 10minute summary to a 40minute deep dive with detailed examples and context what makes it different is the adaptive learning plan you tell it what kind of person you want to become or what youre struggling with and it builds a structured roadmap that evolves with you theres also a virtual coach called freedia that you can chat with anytime to get book recommendations clarify ideas or explore new topics the voice options are surprisingly addictive too you can pick anything from a deep calm tone to something more energetic depending on your mood perfect for fitting real learning into commutes or workouts without the usual doomscrolling consume different inputs deliberately you become the average of what you consume not just food but information conversations media if youre watching the same netflix shows and scrolling the same feeds and having the same conversations youre just reinforcing your current identity actively seek out content from people living the life you want follow different creators read different genres join different communities your brain literally cannot generate thoughts outside the raw materials you give it this isnt about toxic positivity or avoiding reality its about expanding your reference points for whats possible when you see someone who used to be like you but changed dramatically it updates your beliefs about what youre capable of most people stay stuck because changing feels like betraying themselves but that version of you that youre so loyal to its already changed a thousand times since childhood you just didnt notice because it happened slowly the only difference now is youre choosing the direction consciously thats not fake thats actually the most authentic thing you can do youre not discovering yourself youre deciding yourself big difference

the architectural identity of san francisco between its victorian past and the future san francisco is widely recognized for an architectural landscape shaped by constant dialogue between history and innovation the citys built environment reflects layers of time where ornate victorian houses stand alongside daring contemporary structures this contrast is not accidental it is the result of geography historical events economic shifts and a persistent desire to reinvent urban space while preserving a distinctive visual character the victorian era left an especially strong imprint on san francisco following the gold rush rapid population growth fueled the construction of elaborate wooden homes designed to display prosperity and craftsmanship decorative facades bay windows steep roofs and rich color palettes became defining features of entire neighborhoods despite devastating earthquakes and fires these buildings survived through restoration efforts becoming symbols of continuity and resilience today they create a recognizable streetscape that attracts visitors and serves as a reminder of the citys nineteenthcentury ambitions at the same time san francisco has never remained frozen in the past modern architecture entered the city through waves of technological and economic change steel glass and concrete reshaped the skyline especially in commercial districts highrise an introduction to your cognitive state understanding the 5 certx variables introduction your minds dashboard welcome to a new way of thinking about thinking itself imagine having a dashboard for your minda set of dials that could show you at any given moment the precise state of your cognitive system this is the core idea behind the certx state space a powerful model for understanding the inner workings of any thinking system whether its a human mind a team of people or a sophisticated ai this document will introduce you to the five core variables of this dashboard coherence c entropy e resonance r temperature t and substrate coupling x by understanding these five dials in simple relatable terms you can gain a deeper insight into your own mental states from moments of brilliant clarity to periods of frustrating confusion lets begin with the first variable which measures the harmony of your thoughts coherence 1 c is for coherence the harmony of your thoughts what is coherence coherence c is the degree of consistency and integration among your thoughts and ideas it measures how well all the different parts of your mind are working together toward a unified understanding a realworld analogy the orchestra think of your mind as an orchestra high coherence is like a wellrehearsed symphony every musician is playing from the same sheet music their instruments are in tune and they follow the conductors lead playing in harmony the result is a beautiful cohesive piece of music low coherence is like an orchestra where every musician decides to play a different song at the same time the result is not music but noisea confusing and contradictory clash of sounds what coherence feels like your state of coherence can range from fragmented to overly rigid coherence states too low fragmented too high rigid fragmented rigid contradictory dogmatic confused especially when entropy is high unable to update beliefs risk of schizophrenic fragmentation while the harmony of coherence is essential a healthy mind also needs to explore new melodies and ideas this brings us to our next variable entropy 2 e is for entropy the engine of exploration what is entropy entropy e is the measure of exploration in your thinking high entropy means you are considering many different possibilities and pathways while low entropy means you are focused on refining just a few select ideas a realworld analogy brainstorming vs finalizing imagine you are working on a new project high entropy is the initial brainstorming phase you and your team fill a whiteboard with countless ideassome practical some wild some seemingly impossible the goal is to explore the entire landscape of possibilities without judgment low entropy is the final phase of writing the project report you have selected the single best idea and are now narrowly focused on executing it refining the details and ensuring every word is perfect what entropy feels like your state of entropy can range from being stuck in a rut to feeling lost in chaos entropy states too low stuck too high chaotic repetitive chaotic stuck in narrow patterns overwhelmed depressed unable to decide or commit bored as you explore new ideas with entropy some of those ideas will begin to connect and gain momentum this phenomenon is measured by resonance 3 r is for resonance the power of patterns what is resonance resonance r is the degree to which your thoughts and patterns reinforce one another its a measure of harmonic alignment where ideas that are in phase with each other begin to amplify and strengthen creating dominant themes in your thinking a realworld analogy the echo chamber resonance can be both a powerful tool and a dangerous trap healthy resonance is like a recurring helpful theme in a great story it gives the narrative depth and connects different parts of the plot making the whole story feel more meaningful and cohesive dangerously high resonance is like an echo chamber a single idea whether true or not gets repeated and amplified until it drowns out all other perspectives this can lead to rigid selfreinforcing loops that are disconnected from reality a dangerous condition known as a fossil state what resonance feels like your state of resonance can range from scattered and disconnected to obsessive and stuck resonance states too low scattered too high obsessive disconnected stuck in a repetitive loop scattered in an echo chamber no themes emerge at risk of a fossil state a rigid loop disconnected from reality caused by high resonance combined with low coherence the energy of these repeating patterns contributes to the overall volatility of your cognitive system which is measured by temperature 4 t is for temperature the systems volatility what is temperature temperature t is the measure of volatility or jitteriness in your thinking high temperature means your mind is energetic and open to new risky and potentially transformative ideas while low temperature means your thinking is more stable predictable and conservative a realworld analogy the scientist think of a scientist in a laboratory a hightemperature state is like a scientist trying a radical new experiment its risky and has a high chance of failure but it could also lead to a worldchanging breakthrough this state is essential for discovery a lowtemperature state is like the same scientist meticulously replicating a known result its a stable predictable and lowrisk process that ensures quality and consistency but doesnt lead to new discoveries what temperature feels like your state of temperature can range from feeling frozen and riskaverse to feeling erratic and unstable temperature states too low frozen too high unstable extremely stable chaotic predictable unreliable riskaverse erratic depressed angry anxious with all of this internal activityharmonizing exploring and vibrating with energya thinking system needs a firm connection to its foundation this crucial anchor is substrate coupling 5 x is for substrate coupling your anchor in reality what is substrate coupling substrate coupling x measures how strongly your thinking is tethered to your foundational knowledge core values and external reality it is the grounding force that ensures your mind for all its exploration remains connected to what is true and important a realworld analogy the kite a healthy cognitive system is like a kite flying on a windy day the kite is your mind free to soar explore new heights and dance in the currents of new ideas the string is substrate coupling connecting the kite to you on the ground if the string is too short high x the kite cant get off the ground and is inflexible your thinking is rigid and unable to adapt if the string breaks low x the kite flies away chaotically becoming untethered and lost your thinking becomes ungrounded and disconnected from reality what substrate coupling feels like your state of substrate coupling determines whether you feel grounded and flexible or disconnected and rigid substrate coupling states too low ungrounded too high inflexible disconnected from reality rigidly bound to training hallucinating inflexible anxious unable to adapt to new info angry contributes to fossil states where thinking becomes decoupled from reality these five variables provide a rich vocabulary for describing your inner world but their true power and the beauty of this model emerges when you see how they dance together conclusion the dance of a healthy mind these five variables dont exist in isolation they are in a constant dynamic dance a healthy effective mind is not one that keeps all the dials locked in one place but one that moves fluidly between different states in a purposeful rhythm this rhythm is called breathing a healthy mind breathes by oscillating between two key phases 1 the expansion phase entropy e rises as you explore and generate solution candidates coherence c naturally lowers to allow for this creative divergence 2 the compression phase coherence c rises as you integrate what youve learned find patterns and synthesize insights entropy e naturally lowers as you focus the experience of having all five variables in their optimal rangesof breathing smoothly between exploration and integration with healthy resonance stable temperature and strong groundingis something many of us have felt before its often described as a flow state a period of peak performance effortless focus and deep wellbeing by understanding c e r t and x you gain more than just a new set of terms you gain a new language to be curious and compassionate about your own mind a dashboard to understand its intricate dance and a map to navigateand even improveyour own remarkable cognitive world

their influence on one another if the org chart is the organizations skeleton the mesh is its living nervous systemthe network of realtime signals feedback loops and learned reflexes that determines how it actually moves and behaves this perspective moves beyond the rigid lines of a formal chart to capture the realtime flow of information influence and energy that truly drives outcomes it reveals the informal networks the crossfunctional collaborations and the hidden bottlenecks that define an organizations actual operating model the health of this mesh once the domain of intuition can now be precisely measured 3 a new dashboard for organizational health the five core metrics the unified framework provides a quantifiable way to assess organizational health in realtime these are not abstract theories they are the core dimensions of a state space that has been empirically validated in six different domains including ai training and financial market strategy they function as lead indicators of performance and resilience allowing leaders to gain unprecedented insight and intervene with precision framework metric business application interpretation coherence c strategic alignment focus coherence measures the degree of consistency across the organizations agents the optimal range c 065075 represents a state of flexible focus where teams are strategically aligned but not so rigid that they stifle innovation low coherence indicates fragmentation and conflicting priorities high coherence signals dogmatic rigidity and an inability to adapt entropy e capacity for innovation exploration entropy measures the systems exploration of new ideas and possibilities a healthy organization does not have a fixed ideal entropy rather it oscillates periods of high entropy are necessary for brainstorming and innovation while periods of low entropy are required for focused execution a constantly low entropy indicates stagnation constantly high entropy indicates chaos resonance r cultural momentum pattern reinforcement resonance measures the selfreinforcement of ideas and behaviors high resonance is a powerful force for building a strong positive culture however it becomes dangerous when coherence is low leading to the formation of toxic echo chambers and departmental silos that reinforce their own logic against company strategy temperature t organizational agility risk appetite temperature is a measure of the systems volatility and willingness to adapt it reflects the capacity for change and appetite for risk for example in complex reasoning tasks the optimal temperature has been validated at t07 a state where the system operates at peak computational capacity high temperature is required for transformation while a lower temperature supports stable execution substrate coupling x grounding in core values mission this metric measures the organizations connection to its foundational principlesits core mission values and market realities it is the anchor that prevents strategic drift when substrate coupling is low teams become untethered from customer needs and core business objectives pursuing misaligned goals while these five metrics provide a multifaceted view the framework reveals a single paramount measure of systemic health the critical damping ratio 12 this is not a management target it is a universal constant for healthy dynamics discovered independently by three separate ai systems and observed across all tested domains it is a fundamental law of resilient systems think of it as the suspension in a highperformance vehicle an underdamped system 1 is like a car with bouncy shocksit overreacts to every bump and becomes unstable an overdamped system 1 is like a truck with no suspensionsluggish and unresponsive the optimal state of 12 is a finely tuned suspension that is slightly overdamped it absorbs shocks without sacrificing agility keeping the vehicle stable responsive and in control achieving and maintaining this critical ratio is the key to building an organization that is both resilient and agile this state of dynamic stability is sustained by a healthy operational rhythm 4 the rhythm of high performance the breathing cycle of innovation and execution our diagnostics reveal the most common failure mode in modern organizations a breakdown in the systems physical breathing rhythm which fatally separates exploration from execution teams are either stuck in endless ideation that leads nowhere or are so focused on execution that they fail to innovate mastering the natural rhythm between these two modes is a core strategic objective the framework defines this essential cadence as breathing dynamics an oscillation between two distinct operational phases the expansion phase this is the mode for exploration brainstorming and generating new ideas it is characterized by relaxed constraints lower coherence and a high capacity for exploration higher entropy the goal is not to be right but to generate a wide range of possibilities the compression phase this is the mode for integration decisionmaking and execution it is characterized by convergence on solutions higher coherence and reduced exploration lower entropy the goal is to evaluate possibilities make clear commitments and align on a path forward this mixture of modes is the single greatest source of energy drain we measure in dysfunctional teams forcing a team to ideate and decide simultaneously ensures neither is done well the framework provides a clear and powerful intervention actionable strategy restructuring a breathing cadence to restore a healthy rhythm leaders must rigorously separate these two modes of work especially in how meetings are structured expansion meetings purpose to brainstorm explore possibilities and diverge rules no decisions are allowed wild ideas are encouraged the focus is on building upon not critiquing suggestions outputs a list of unevaluated possibilities and new avenues for exploration compression meetings purpose to decide commit and align for execution rules no new ideas are introduced the agenda is strictly limited to evaluating the options generated in a prior expansion phase outputs clear decisions concrete action items and assigned responsibilities the core principle is absolute never mix the two meeting types when this healthy rhythm breaks down entirely the organization risks a state of pathological rigidity 5 diagnosing and healing organizational rigidity the fossil state the framework offers a powerful diagnostic for deepseated organizational dysfunction the artificial fossil this is not a metaphor for being stuck it is a precisely defined pathological state a system enters when it becomes rigid selfreinforcing its own internal logic while becoming dangerously disconnected from reality it is the datadriven signature of thats how weve always done it and its mathematical fingerprint is r 085 with c 05 the characteristics of a fossil state map directly onto common intractable business problems high resonance r low coherence c this is the signature of toxic echo chambers and departmental silos each group reinforces its own logic high r that directly conflicts with overall company strategy low c leading to political polarization and a breakdown of crossfunctional collaboration low substrate coupling x this manifests as teams or entire business units that have become disconnected from core values customer needs or market realities they operate on outdated assumptions and are resistant to feedback that contradicts their ingrained model no breathing the system is stuck it cannot enter an expansion phase to explore new ideas or a compression phase to execute effectively this results in bureaucratic inertia analysis paralysis and a culture that punishes deviation from established norms the primary intervention to break a fossil state is thermal annealing in business terms this means intentionally increasing the systems temperature volatility and diversity of input to break the rigid pattern and allow a healthier one to form concrete examples of this strategy include injecting diverse perspectives by bringing in outside experts or rotating team members creating crossfunctional skunkworks teams to tackle a problem with fresh eyes free from existing constraints encouraging and structuring dissent through red team exercises to challenge ingrained assumptions and test the resilience of a strategy by carefully raising the temperature leaders can melt away rigidities allowing the organization to reform around a more coherent and realitygrounded state this moves beyond simply fixing problems to proactively building a culture of resilience 6 the competitive advantage of a meshaware culture building a meshaware organization is not merely about improving operational efficiency it is about cultivating a sustainable competitive advantage through superior adaptability innovation and resilience this approach provides a datadriven blueprint for designing a culture that thrives on complexity the core principles are as follows 1 foster psychological safety to encourage exploration psychological safety is the primary cultural mechanism for reducing the energy cost of increasing entropy e a culture where individuals feel safe to propose wild ideas makes exploration efficient not just permissible this safety is the prerequisite for the expansion phase of breathing e the engine of all innovation 2 reinforce a clear and coherent mission a powerful wellcommunicated mission and set of core values provides the essential grounding for the organization x and the strategic focus needed for execution c this ensures that when the organization shifts to its compression phase its energy is channeled toward a shared meaningful purpose 3 build a symbolic immune system this involves creating clear cultural norms and rapid response protocols to address toxicity misinformation and other pathogens that threaten collective coherence by identifying and neutralizing behaviors that lead to fossilization early the culture protects itself before dysfunction can become entrenched 4 champion the rhythm of breathing the leaders most crucial role is to protect the sanctity of both expansion and compression cycles this means creating and defending time for pure exploration free from the pressure of immediate results while also enforcing the discipline required for decisive execution by treating culture as a dynamic system that can be measured and guided this physicsbased approach provides a far more powerful and reliable methodology than traditional intuitionbased efforts 7 conclusion your first steps as a meshaware leader the unified framework provides a fundamentally new and actionable model for executive leadership it moves the art of management closer to a science providing a new dashboard to see understand and influence the deep dynamics that truly govern organizational life leadership is no longer just the art of managing people it is the science of tuning a living systems fundamental dynamics the question is no longer what should we do but what physical state must we achieve applying these principles can begin today with three practical steps 1 reframe your meetings implement a strict separation between expansion brainstorming exploration and compression decisionmaking execution meetings this single change can immediately reduce meeting fatigue and dramatically improve the quality of both innovation and execution 2 conduct a fossil hunt identify one area of the business stuck in how weve always done it and design a smallscale thermal annealing experiment such as commissioning a pilot project with a diverse crossfunctional team to reexamine the issue from the ground up 3 start measuring team health introduce the concept of a bloomline checkin to begin assessing team alignment coherence and the balance of exploration vs execution breathing this opens the door to a new datainformed conversation about team dynamics and performance

sunday serenity grounding your energy for a peaceful week welcome to sunday serenity a day to anchor ourselves in the present moment and cultivate a sense of inner peace that will carry us through the week lets move beyond just rest and delve into grounding practices that connect us to our core finding your center sunday is a perfect time to realign our energy and find our center lets explore ways to ground ourselves earth connection spend time outdoors connecting with nature walk barefoot on the grass sit beneath a tree or simply observe the beauty around you visualize your roots extending deep into the earth grounding you and providing stability how will you connect with the earth today body awareness practice a grounding meditation focusing on the sensations of your body and the feeling of being present engage in mindful movement such as gentle stretching or a slow deliberate walk take note of your posture and gently correct it mindful breathing practice deep slow breaths allowing your body to relax and your mind to quiet visualize your breath as an anchor grounding you in the present moment set a timer and practice deep breathing for a few minutes setting intentions with clarity instead of overwhelming yourself with todo lists set clear and concise intentions for the week focus on intentions that align with your values and promote your wellbeing write down 3 intentions for the upcoming week creating a calming ritual prepare a warm beverage and enjoy it mindfully savoring each sip listen to calming music or create a playlist of your favorite soothing sounds light a candle and allow the gentle flame to create a sense of peace anchoring your peace what grounding practices resonate with you how will you cultivate a sense of serenity today share your experiences and insights in the comments below creating a collective space for grounding and peace

anki for complex topics my approach and templates ive seen this question coming up often enough that it merits sharing this collection of internal notes documenting my approach to anki hope it helps you during your studies stay safe and be kind to each other tldr a sample gallery for mobile cards can be seen on a sample gallery for desktop cards can be seen on clozed cards look something like this you can change the theme toggling the side button on the top right corner see the different lightdark mode themes on and you can change the zoom level tapping on the context field see the different sizes on mobile screen on find both a spanish and an english versions of the templates on if at your zoom level mathjax seems too wide for the box but without overflowing it scroll the box itself horizontally to see it in full introduction disclaimer my work is heavily inspired on the work of both michael nielsen1 and luke thorburn2 if you are not aware of their work its a short read and provides some context for what follows in particular check lukes for the templates i based my cards on when one thinks of flashcards srs or anki one might at first think that such learning methods are just suitable for language or trivia facts oneliner front and back and thats it right just rote memorisation ahead of us nicely spaced repetitions sure but where is actual knowledge and understanding to be found can one learn advanced topics on maths physics or even philosophy with all their intricacies and complexity is it possible to bend anki and make it work to build up a net of interconnected pieces of knowledge with true understanding of them we already find ourselves recalling from memory when having studied these concepts under traditional means and we would find it hard to find someone who describes themselves as merely regurgitating memorised facts can we deconstruct such knowledge into simple frontback flashcards i will describe several scenarios that may come up while studying under traditional means and how one could ankify that specific part of the learning process effectively while avoiding rote memorisation i will be referring to my note types along the way then we will have a section for the actual note types their fields and what cards are generated from them finally an ankification loop to ensure proper regular encoding throughout the text most examples will be picked from 1st2nd year undergraduate level mathematics and some philosophy of mathematics but you should still be able to go through the text without missing anything if you were to not know much on this already if you are already studying such subjects at this level you are already familiar with the definitionexamplepropositiontheorem loop you go around and around while in class most of the advise here also works with penandpaper studying and apart from making the cards could be taken asis knowledge and learning theory examples are the definition takefor example the abstract definition of a group on one hand one must know the exact definition to the t one cannot just forget about associativity when providing the full definition but are terms in mathematics defined just because or in context unless you support a pure formalist view of mathematics we are not merely playing a symbol game when doing mathematics and so such context is quite relevant what are some key examples that were the drivers of us defining such term what are some key counterexamples on which some of the definition premises fail one can encode such information on the 0 definicindefinition note type which includes dedicated counterexample fields as well as preguntarespuesta lmiteedge case question answer 13 fields which may be used to encode extra counterexamples and their relation to the hypothesis history and visualisation algebra is the offer made by the devil to the mathematician the devil says i will give you this powerful machine it will answer any question you like all you need to do is give me your soul give up geometry and you will have this marvellous machine sir michael francis atiyah sure if you are on a maths undergrad you are likely good at the formalist game and can work around the algebra for most proofs given the definitions particularly in say intro courses on linearabstract algebra but what does this tell you about the objects of study did you really learn anything new about them while working out the proof or it just works algebraically and so it is true and you learn a theorem statement by rote memory one cannot substitute formal rigor for geometric intuition but having one without the other is a bit like a bowl of cereal without milk you will end up with a dry hard ball to swallow by force as for history i find it quite important to contextualise definitionstheorem in the time they were stated most of mathematics has been rooted in geometric basisintuition until relatively recently proofs usually being a geometric argument that we may nowadays agree or not on the rigour not distributing terms along an equation one should try to answer the following questions what problem was the person who invented this trying to solve what was the contemporary knowledge of the subject at the time how did the statementdefinition evolve into its current form as a classical example the modern formulation of galois theory has nothing to do with galois original formulation despite the power of our current version its no wonder that most students take a course on it and leave feeling they havent really grasped the solauded link galois made see this as an example also mind one of the responses also noting you should also always look for good memorable examples linking back to our previous point about examples any note type may do for this particularly the ones with fields intuicinintuition and preguntarespuesta lmiteedge case qa deconstructing proofsarguments rote memorisation of any proof or argument is futile however there are 2 distillation phases from which depending on the complexity one should be able to reconstruct the full argument on the fly ie filling in the gaps first most proofs one encounters are predicated on a single key idea take the definition of a group again it guarantees there is an inverse of each element but not its uniqueness do we really have to memorise each and every single algebraic step for the uniqueness proof however simple it is or shall we just remember that its a proof by contradiction assuming 2 such inverses existed we show they must be the same actually and be able to reproduce it in full whenever needed this is where the idea clavekey idea excels one can encode such information on this field and for around 80 of propositionstheorems this will be enough now say you are taking a real analysis course and are facing your first encounter with an epsilondelta proof it is already daunting to go through it how am i to reduce it to a single sentence well just dont dont use a hammer for everything instead try to deconstruct it into 56 discrete steps not just merely with algebraic manipulations on them but with the why you are doing such step too if you can recall that the algebraic manipulation for that individual step should come pretty easy do include the algebraic manipulation on the step too but do not make it the key part of it the enumerarenumerate note type will then create cards for each individual step covering it while still displaying the others as well as a card for the whole process once you have internalised and fully understood how an epsilondelta proof goes you will find that you can then encode later proofs into the key idea field instead of a whole enumerate card say you have to prove that the sum of cauchy sequences is cauchy a proof where you get to a final 2 bound but can then go back to the original bound to make it 2 2 you may encode that as standard epsilondelta proof once we get the 2 bound go back and make it 2 regardless of the note type you use for this there are several questions that you should try to answer and encode in edge case questionanswer what happens if we change one or more of the premises what happens if we remove the premise completely what alternative proofs can be found for this statement if at all do they follow a fundamentally different process how does the proof itself connect to the subject at hand or other related ones minimal information principle anyone not familiar with piotr wozniak and his 20 rules should just stop reading here and come back later i will not expand on this much more but it is important enough that it must be mentioned as a rule of thumb most cards shouldnt take more than 1520s to answer dont feel pressed though but dont take more than 1min even with these complex topics exceptions are the whole definitiontheoremenumeration cards which might take longer and you may find some pen and paper at hand useful to avoid juggling everyting in your mind if its taking you longer than that you are doubting on the answer too much thats a sign that the card is a bad card flag it and take some time afterwards to reflect on it could you break it down into even more cards to make it cognitively simpler did you just ask chatgpt to make cards for you and you didnt previously understand yourself the content and are just trying to forcefully memorise it instead this is an everevolving personal process though you will find what works and what doesnt over time as you get familiar with encoding this kind of information into anki cards be ready to remake a note over and over if you feel it isnt right this is not lost time its knowledge you gain if you edit the card its because youve recognised an inherent limitation on its current content gaining an understanding that may not have taken place if you had not taken the time to make the card in the first place templates this is a nonexhaustive description of note types and cards created from them
